speaker: Doctor

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand your concern; the combination of hematuria and right flank pain with a history of recurrent UTIs raises suspicion for a stone or infection. Have you noticed any fever or chills accompanying this pain? REQUEST TEST: Urine Culture. REQUEST TEST: Serum Creatinine.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urine Culture: Pending; Serum Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL

speaker: Doctor
text: I see your creatinine is normal, which is reassuring for kidney function. Do you notice any passage of a small, gritty stone or "sand" in your urine, or does the pain come in sharp waves?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history except noted recurrent urinary tract infections. No history of renal dialysis or known genetic diseases. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works in an office setting.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any nausea, vomiting, or fever alongside this right-sided pain? REQUEST TEST: Urine_Culture. REQUEST TEST: Non-Contrast_KT_Abdomen_Pelvis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal imaging results and lack of systemic signs like fever, the recurrent history of UTIs alongside right flank pain strongly suggests a specific type of kidney stone formation. Do you have a history of straining or noticing any dark, sand-like particles in your urine? DIAGNOSIS READY: Calcium Oxalate Nephrolithiasis
